review.hazards_note: H1 identifies the correct magnitude issue, but its check unnecessarily mandates 64-bit integer storage and arithmetic; require exact, overflow-safe representation of heights, products, and residuals, allowing other sufficiently precise representations. Add a conditional precision check for square-root/quadratic-boundary calculations: computed floor/ceil roots and candidate core sizes must satisfy their defining inequalities, including zero and perfect-square cases. H2 is appropriate.
review.editorial_note: No END route follows the reference's scan over b, setting t=h-(n-b), selecting a cardinality with N11/N12, and greedily constructing the increasing block inside a decreasing outer prefix. The relevant ingredients exist separately, but their parameter search and correctness invariant are absent. In adding this route, do not copy the editorial's unrestricted canonical-height formula: an increasing subset omitting b leaves b to increase the height in the suffix, and the outer maximum must also be considered. The reference needs the additional fact that its first successful b makes the greedy subset contain b; together with h>=2n-1, this validates its target equation.

The reference scan's first-success invariant: writing m for the least index with m(m-1)>=h-n, its first successful b is m unless the resulting deficit is 2, in which case it is m+1 when available. The successful right-to-left greedy subset contains b, which is necessary for the claimed canonical height; connect these facts to the cardinality test and failure condition.
review.editorial_note: N11/N12 capture the editorial's fixed-cardinality subproblem, but none of the END routes follows its varying-b scan and canonical output construction. P3 fixes the additive construction around cup n, while P5 chooses and repairs the core directly rather than establishing the scan's invariants. Also, the editorial's unrestricted canonical height formula is false: when the selected set contains b, the correct height is max(2n-1,n-b+sum(2x-1)); if b is omitted, the descending remainder can create an additional maximum. The reference is safe because of its first successful b and its particular greedy witness, so those invariants—not the unrestricted editorial lemmas—should support the added route.

N23 and N24 provide the qualifications that make the reference implementation valid.
